title: Preventing Cross-border Transmission of HMPV from Becoming Public Health Concern in Singapore
what_it_is: Preventing Cross-border Transmission of HMPV from Becoming Public Health Concern in Singapore

sections.label: HMPV activity and preventive advice
sections.summary: Singapore observed increased HMPV activity year-end, with no vaccine available, so the public is advised to take preventive measures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: In Singapore, based on our ongoing surveillance for acute respiratory diseases, we also have observed an increase in HMPV activity during the year-end period, similar to previous years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: There are currently no vaccines for HMPV and the influenza vaccine does not provide protection against HMPV infection.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary) (for the Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Similar to other respiratory infections, the advice to the public and especially medically vulnerable persons, such as young children, the elderly and those with chronic medical conditions, is to take preventive measures, such as the practice of good personal hygiene, limiting social contacts when sick and seeing a doctor promptly if symptoms worsen.

sections.label: Subsidised flu vaccine eligibility groups
sections.summary: A GP said MOH's fully subsidised annual flu vaccine under Healthier SG goes only to higher-risk groups.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: My second supplementary question is that, under Healthier SG, the general practitioner shared with me that MOH's fully subsidised annual flu vaccine are only given to the higher-risk groups under five and above 65, with respiratory-related chronic diseases.

sections.label: Reviewing national vaccination programme criteria
sections.summary: MOH regularly reviews criteria for national vaccination programmes and subsidised Healthier SG programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For the second question, indeed, we do regularly review the criteria for national vaccination programmes and for programmes under Healthier SG that are subsidised.

sections.label: Alerts and advice for respiratory diseases
sections.summary: Criteria are always reviewed, and alerts are issued when a specific action like vaccination is needed; otherwise advice stays the same.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: The short answer to her question, we will always be reviewing the criteria that we use for these types of programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In general, when we are considering what are the things to put an SMS alert or some kind of alert out to the population, it is where there is a specific action that they need to take, such as going and getting a vaccination for the new season's variants of influenza, where there is a vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: For respiratory diseases where there is no vaccine, whether it is a variant or different variant or whatever the species of virus is, the advice is the same.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is the same throughout the year, which is: to practise good personal hygiene; do not go and mix with people when you are sick; and if symptoms worsen, seek medical care.
